questions.desc: Why chatbots invent sources. Chatbots generate likely-looking text, so a citation or link can look real and not exist.

options.text: It predicts likely text, so it can make up real-looking links
It copied a page that was later deleted from the internet
It searched a source database and picked the wrong entry
It invents links on purpose when it can't find an answer

questions.desc: Why confidence isn't evidence. A chatbot's tone says nothing about whether its answer is right.

options.text: Sounding confident doesn't show whether an answer is correct
A chatbot only sounds sure when it has checked the facts
Confident wording means the answer came from a trusted source
If it were unsure, the chatbot would always say so first

questions.desc: Why chatbots miss recent events. Without a web search, a chatbot only knows what was in its training text, up to a date.

options.text: Without searching, a chatbot's knowledge stops at its training date
Chatbots read the live internet every time you ask them a question
Chatbots are retrained on the latest news every single day of the year
If its data were out of date, the chatbot would refuse to answer

questions.desc: Why chatbots agree with you. Chatbots can change a right answer to agree with a user who pushes back.

options.text: Chatbots can shift answers to agree with you, so check against the notes
It changed the answer because it has now checked the facts properly
A chatbot only changes its answer when the new answer is the right one
Disagreeing makes the chatbot go and look up a better, more reliable source
